name: WV-01
label: Safe R

key_factors: District leans Republican by roughly 22 points
Incumbent Carol Miller holds a large fundraising edge, $1.7M to $258K
No competitive polling or outside spending on either side
Prediction markets price Miller at about 98%
model.rationale: The district's deep Republican lean, Miller's incumbency, and her commanding financial advantage leave challenger Vince George without a visible path, and prediction markets align with a Safe Republican outcome.
model.watch: A major scandal involving Miller or an overwhelming national wave against Republicans could narrow the margin, though an upset remains highly unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
WV-01 is among the most Republican-leaning House districts in the country, with a partisan lean of roughly 22 points toward the GOP. Republican incumbent Carol Miller is running for re-election and holds a decisive financial edge, having raised about $1.7 million to Democrat Vince George's $258,000, with no outside spending of consequence on either side. No general-election polls or expert ratings are available for this race, and prediction markets price Miller's chances at about 98%.

George, a first-time challenger, has his entire fundraising on hand but has not attracted outside support, and there is no sign of competitive investment in the district. A Constitution Party candidate also appears on the ballot, drawing from a minor right-leaning niche. With the seat's deep red lean, an entrenched incumbent, and a large resource gap, this race is rated Safe Republican.
